newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX May Brent falls, tracking NYMEX.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX May Brent falls, tracking NYMEX.

text.p: SIMEX Brent May crude futures were expected to ease further, catching up with losses on late NYMEX trade, brokers said on Thursday.
Brokers said in the last trading hour on NYMEX, the prompt WTI contract shed a further 40 cents, extending the day's already sharp technically driven losses on IPE Brent.

Late Wednesday, IPE May Brent ended down some 60 cents at $18.51 per barrel, breaking its key technical support of $19.00. The new level is also a new eight month low, well below the triple bottom of $18.67 from July 29, 1996.
At 0355 GMT, May futures were quoted at $18.15/$18.30.
"SIMEX is making up for the losses seen on the last one hour trade on WTI," said one broker.
He said he expected the May contract on SIMEX to shed by another 10 to 20 cents to around $18.20-$18.25 per barrel.
WTI contract on ACCESS, NYMEX overnight trading system, was last quoted at $19.55 per barrel, eights cents up from its last closed on shortcovering, brokers said.
They said the downtrend remained intact.
